 ORAL JUDGMENT 1.

The present First Appeal, under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, is preferred by the appellant/s - original claimant/s - legal heirs of the deceased - Rajendrakumar Champaklal Shah,
being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the common judgment and award dated 29.08.2011 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Aux.), Vadodara in Motor Accident Claim Petition No. 148 of 1994, by which the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.3,78,215/- with 7.5% per annum interest to the claimant/s, holding Opponents No.2 and 3 i.e. owner and insurance company of the Tempo No.GJ-17-T-5464 liable, jointly and severally.

sentences.text: It is noted that the Tribunal has exonerated opponents No.4 and 5 i.e. owner and insurance company of the Ambulance from the liability.

2. Brief facts of the case are as under:
2.1 That on 19.10.1993 at about 10:00 p.m., deceased - Rajendrakumar was travelling in the Ambulance Van bearing registration No.GJ-6-T-9932, driven by opponent No.4, to hand over the dead-body to Naswadi.

While returning, the ambulance van was going on its correct side of the road and when it reached near the place of occurrence, at that time, NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1489/2012 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined opponent No.1 - driver came from opposite direction by driving Tempo bearing registration No.GJ-17-T-5464 in rash and negligent manner on wrong side of the road i.e.
Arunaben Wd/O Rajendrakumar ... vs Deleted on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23521095/
2 towards ambulance side and gave violent impact to the ambulance.
As a result, the ambulance after turning round went into a drainage and the persons travelling therein sustained fatal injuries.

Therefore, the legal heirs of the deceased - widow,
two children and mother have filed claim petition seeking compensation of Rs.20 lakhs with cost and interest for unnatural and untimely death against the present respondents before the Tribunal.
2.2 Notices were served to the opponents.
Opponent No.1 - driver was deleted, as was not available.
Opponents 2 and 4 i.e. owner of the tempo and driver of the ambulance van have not filed their written statement before the Tribunal.

Opponent No.3 - Insurance Company of the Tempo and opponent No.5 and 6 - Vadodara Municipal Corporation - owner of the Ambulance and opponent No.6 - insurance company of the ambulance van have appeared and filed their written statements / objections, by disputing all the averments made by the claimant in the claim petition.
2.3 The Tribunal has framed the issues.
The oral as well as documentary evidence were led by the rival parties NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1489/2012 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024
undefined before the Tribunal.
After considering the documentary as well as oral evidence and submissions made at the bar, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition by awarding compensation as noted above.

2.4 Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal,
the present appeal is preferred by the claimant/s for enhancement.
3.1 Learned advocate Mr. Hakim for the appellant/s - claimant/s has submitted that the Tribunal has committed an error in not properly calculating the amount of compensation.

He has submitted that amount of award is on lower side as the Tribunal has not properly considered the various aspects; like prospective income of the deceased, negligence, liability and family circumstances, etc.
He has submitted that the deceased was aged about only 39 years at the time of accident and was doing business in the name of New Janata Readymade Stores.
He has submitted that at the relevant point of time, his monthly income was Rs.4,554/-, which is considered by the Tribunal and there is no dispute about it.
He has submitted that the Tribunal has not considered the prospective income of the deceased, which should be considered 40% in view of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court.

He has fairly submitted that the learned Tribunal has NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1489/2012 JUDGMENT DATED:
13/09/2024 undefined rightly considered the deduction of personal expenses looking to the age of the deceased and multiplier.

He has submitted that therefore, considering the loss of dependency, it would be calculated as Rs.4,554/- as monthly income plus 40% as prospective income minus 1/4th for personal expenses multiplied by 12 months and multiplied by 15 multiplier would come to Rs.8,60,715/- total loss of dependency, which should be awarded to the claimants by the learned Tribunal.

3.2 He has further submitted that considering the general and non-pecuniary damages,
the learned Tribunal should award Rs.18,150/- each towards loss of estate and funeral expenses.

He has also submitted that towards loss of consortium, there are four dependents and therefore, it would be awarded Rs.1,93,600/- should be awarded as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of United India Insurance Co. Ltd., versus Satinder Kaur @

sentences.text: Tempo has submitted that the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is just and proper.
The Tribunal has rightly considered the income of the deceased, the age of the deceased, the dependency and future aspect of income.
He has submitted that under the head of loss of estate and funeral expenses, the Tribunal has rightly awarded compensation.
He has submitted that the amount under the head of loss of consortium is just and proper.
He has submitted that this appeal may be dismissed and no interference be made by this Court.

4.2 Learned advocate Mr.Haresh J. Trivedi for Vadodara Municipal Corporation and learned advocate Mr.Sunil Parikh for the respondent - insurance company of the Ambulance Van have submitted that the Tribunal has exonerated them and there is no liability fastened upon them.
They have submitted that the impugned judgment and award is just and proper and no interference be made by this Court.
5. It is noteworthy to mention that the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 which gives paramount importance to the concept of 'just and fair' compensation.
It is a beneficial legislation which has been framed with the object of providing relief to the victims or their families.

NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1489/2012 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act deals with the concept of 'just compensation' which ought to be determined on the foundation of fairness, reasonableness and equitability.
It also endeavors to make good the human suffering to the extent possible and to also save families which have lost their breadwinners from being pushed to wandering.

Although such determination can never be arithmetically exact or perfect, an endeavor should be made by the Court to award just and fair compensation irrespective of the amount claimed by the claimants.
6.1 I have considered the submissions made by the rival parties.
I have perused the record and proceedings of the Tribunal.
I have gone through the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.

From the record, it transpires that the deceased was aged about 39 years and was doing business in the name of New Janata Readymade Store in Vadodara and his monthly income was Rs.4,554/-, as considered by the Tribunal at the relevant point of time.

Therefore, it should be considered as monthly income of the deceased and accordingly, yearly income would come to Rs.54,648/- and by adding 40% prospective income as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court,
which is not calculated by the learned Tribunal, it would come to Rs.21,859/- and therefore, total income comes to Rs.76,507/- per annum.

Since NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1489/2012 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined the deceased is aged about 39 years and there are four dependents, 1/4th would be proper to be deducted as personal expenses and therefore, it would come to Rs.19,126/-.

Hence, the income would come to Rs.57,381/- per year and applying 15 multiplier as per the schedule of the Motor Vehicles Act as well as the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma versus Delhi Transport Corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, it would come to Rs.8,60,715/- as loss of dependency, which is required to be awarded to the Arunaben Wd/O Rajendrakumar ...

6.2 Further, considering the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Pranay Shethi (supra), as general and non-pecuniary damages, under the head of loss of estate and funeral expenses, if we award Rs.18,150/- and Rs.18,150/-, respectively, which would be the just and proper compensation.
6.3 Further, there are four dependents to the deceased.

Therefore, as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of United India Insurance Co. Ltd., versus Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur reported in (2021) 11 SCC 780, Rs.40,000/- consortium to each dependent and 10% rise, which comes to Rs.48,400/- as consortium to each dependent, which total comes to Rs.1,93,600/-, which should be awarded NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/1489/2012 JUDGMENT DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined to the claimants.

8.1 The appeal is partly allowed.
